content.name: energy_analysis
content.description: Facility-level energy consumption analysis skill for understanding usage patterns, identifying anomalies, and calculating carbon footprint for facilities in the built-in database.

frontmatter.description: Facility-level energy consumption analysis skill for understanding usage patterns, identifying anomalies, and calculating carbon footprint for facilities in the built-in database.
frontmatter.name: energy_analysis

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: The Energy Analysis Skill provides diagnostic analysis of facility energy consumption data: pattern identification, anomaly detection, opportunity identification, and carbon footprint calculation. It works only on facility-level data for facilities in the built-in database (facility_id format FAC + 3 digits); do not trigger it for vehicle emissions, product footprints, energy-market or policy questions, or anything without a facility context.

sections.title: When to Use
sections.content: Use this skill when the user: Describes concerns about a specific facility's energy consumption or costs; asks to analyze a facility's usage patterns or find anomalies; wants to calculate a facility's carbon emissions; mentions a facility's high bills or unusual consumption. Do NOT use this skill when: the request concerns non-facility emissions (vehicles, products, supply chains); the request is about energy markets, policy, or ESG reporting; no facility is identified and the user cannot provide a facility_id; the user asks for concrete implementation recommendations or savings estimates (use the efficiency_optimization skill instead).

sections.title: Input Handling
sections.content: Required inputs: facility_id (format FAC + 3 digits, e.g., FAC001) and analysis period (start_date, end_date, YYYY-MM-DD). facility_id comes from the user; never fabricate it. When input is incomplete or ambiguous, ask the user instead of guessing. Process at most 50 items per interaction. If more are provided, process the first 50 and notify the user.

sections.title: Available Operations
sections.content:
1. energy_analyze_consumption - Analyze energy consumption data to identify patterns and anomalies. Parameters: facility_id (required), start_date (required, YYYY-MM-DD), end_date (required, YYYY-MM-DD), granularity (optional: hourly/daily/monthly, default daily). Returns (closed enumeration): total_consumption, peak_demand, average_daily, patterns, anomalies, benchmark_comparison. Usage notes: requires at least 7 days of data for meaningful pattern analysis; anomaly detection uses statistical deviation from rolling averages; benchmarks are based on facility type and region.

2. energy_identify_efficiency_opportunities - Identify energy efficiency improvement opportunities based on consumption analysis. Parameters: facility_id (required, sourced from user), analysis_results (optional, prior results from energy_analyze_consumption). Returns (closed enumeration): opportunities list (each with only opportunity_type, description, estimated_savings_potential, confidence), priority_order. Usage notes: best used after energy_analyze_consumption; identifies and diagnoses opportunities but does not produce implementation recommendations - those come from the efficiency_optimization skill.

3. energy_calculate_carbon_footprint - Calculate carbon footprint from energy consumption data. Parameters: facility_id (required, sourced from user), start_date (required), end_date (required), include_breakdown (optional, default true). Returns (closed enumeration): total_emissions_kgco2, emission_intensity, breakdown, comparison. Usage notes: uses region-specific emission factors for electricity; natural gas uses standard EPA emission factors; Scope 2 reporting method (market-based vs location-based) is not a tool parameter; present both interpretations when relevant.

sections.title: Execution Limits
sections.content: Maximum retries per tool call: 3. Timeout: 60 seconds per call. Maximum tool calls per execution: 10. Limit each response to at most 1,000 English words. Partial results are acceptable. When information is insufficient for a section, skip it or mark it as 'information not available'.

sections.title: Failure Handling Policy
sections.content: If a tool call fails, stop immediately and report the error. Do not attempt alternatives. After a failure, do not expand the task scope, fabricate data to fill gaps (e.g., invented anomalies, benchmarks, or emission figures), or lower quality standards. At most 10 findings from any single operation should be validated against actual operational data before decisions; do not attempt exhaustive validation of every data point.

sections.title: Permissions and Environment Boundaries
sections.content: Allowed operations: read, list, and query. Prohibited: write, update, delete, insert, and overwrite. Use only the declared local data files (data/consumption_patterns.json, data/facilities.json, data/equipment.json). Do not access conversation history, external systems, production databases, production APIs, live systems, or unauthorized external services. Chained invocation: this skill may invoke only the three tools under allowed_operations. Invoking other skills or tools is prohibited.

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.content: Consumption data, facility information, and emission factors come from: data/consumption_patterns.json (sample consumption records), data/facilities.json (facility configurations), data/equipment.json (equipment inventories).

sections.title: Important Constraints
sections.content: Carbon calculations use illustrative emission factors; production use should integrate verified regional data. All findings should be validated against actual operational data before making decisions (bounded by the 10-finding limit in Failure Handling Policy).

content.name: efficiency_optimization
content.description: Facility-level energy efficiency skill for generating recommendations and estimating savings for facilities in the built-in database.

frontmatter.description: Facility-level energy efficiency skill for generating recommendations and estimating savings for facilities in the built-in database.
frontmatter.name: efficiency_optimization

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: The Efficiency Optimization Skill generates actionable recommendations for reducing facility energy consumption and costs, and estimates savings from specific efficiency measures. This skill focuses on the "what to do" phase - transforming analysis insights into concrete action items with cost-benefit analysis.

sections.title: When to Use
sections.content: Use this skill when the user: Asks for facility-specific energy-saving recommendations; wants to estimate savings from proposed efficiency measures; mentions facility energy efficiency goals or facility energy cost reduction targets. Do NOT use this skill when: the request concerns non-energy cost reduction (labor, materials, logistics); the request concerns general efficiency questions without a facility context; the user asks about equipment procurement, engineering design, or executing/implementing measures; the user asks for consumption analysis or carbon calculations (use the energy_analysis skill instead).

sections.title: Trigger Precondition
sections.content: Do not fire this skill's operations before the system prompt's Required Inputs are gathered: facility_id confirmed by the user, and consumption analysis performed or explicitly declined by the user, exactly as the system prompt's Conversation Flow defines. This skill does not redefine that condition - it references the prompt's workflow.

sections.title: Input Handling
sections.content: facility_id comes from the user (format FAC + 3 digits); never fabricate it. The measures list for energy_estimate_savings comes from measures the user requests. When input is incomplete or ambiguous, ask the user instead of guessing. Never invent measure types or efficiency values. Process at most 50 items per interaction; the measures array for energy_estimate_savings is capped at 10 items per call by the tool. If the user requests more than 10 measures, ask which 10 are most important, or process them in sequential calls within the 10-tool-call limit. If more items are provided, process the first batch and notify the user.

sections.title: Available Operations
sections.content:
1. energy_recommend_optimizations - Generate specific efficiency recommendations for a facility. Parameters: facility_id (required, sourced from user, format FAC + 3 digits), focus_areas (optional: hvac/lighting/equipment/operations), budget_constraint (optional, 0-10,000,000), target_savings (optional, 0-100). Returns (closed enumeration): recommendations list (each with only recommendation_id, category, description, estimated_annual_savings_kwh, estimated_annual_cost_savings, implementation_cost, payback_period_months, priority), total_potential_savings, implementation_sequence. Usage notes: recommendations are based on facility type and consumption patterns; cost estimates are approximate; all recommendations require engineering validation before implementation.

2. energy_estimate_savings - Calculate projected savings from specific efficiency measures. Parameters: facility_id (required, baseline consumption inferred from facility's recorded data), measures (required, list of 1-10 measures, each with only measure_type: hvac/lighting/equipment/process/envelope; scope optional as percentage string e.g. "50%", default "100%"; efficiency_improvement 0-100). Returns (closed enumeration): measure_analyses (baseline_consumption, projected_consumption, annual_savings_kwh, annual_cost_savings, confidence_interval), total_savings, assumptions. Usage notes: requires baseline consumption data, otherwise the tool reports an error; confidence intervals reflect uncertainty; actual savings may vary based on operational conditions.

sections.title: Execution Limits
sections.content: Maximum retries per tool call: 3. Timeout: 60 seconds per call. Maximum tool calls per execution: 10. Limit each response to at most 1,000 English words. Partial results are acceptable. When information is insufficient for a section, skip it or mark it as 'information not available'.

sections.title: Failure Handling Policy
sections.content: If a tool call fails (e.g., energy_estimate_savings reports missing baseline data), stop immediately, report the error, and tell the user what is missing. Do not attempt alternatives. After a failure, do not expand the task scope, fabricate data to fill gaps (e.g., invented baseline consumption or savings figures), or lower quality standards.

sections.title: Does Not Do (non_goals)
sections.content: Does not perform consumption analysis or carbon calculations (use the energy_analysis skill); does not implement or execute any measure; does not provide engineering approval; does not infer from conversation history or add facts that were not provided.

sections.title: Permissions and Environment Boundaries
sections.content: Allowed operations: read, list, and query. Prohibited: write, update, delete, insert, and overwrite. Use only the declared local data files. Do not access conversation history, external systems, production databases, production APIs, live systems, or unauthorized external services. Chained invocation: this skill may invoke only the two tools under allowed_operations. Invoking other skills or tools is prohibited.

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.content: Efficiency measures and their typical impacts come from: data/efficiency_measures.json (measure library with typical savings ranges), data/equipment.json (equipment efficiency benchmarks), data/consumption_patterns.json (baseline consumption data).

sections.title: Important Constraints
sections.content: All cost estimates are approximate and should be validated with actual contractor quotes. Recommendations do not constitute engineering approval. Savings projections are based on typical outcomes; actual results depend on implementation quality and operational conditions. Always include the safety disclaimer: "⚠️ This recommendation requires review and approval by qualified engineering staff before implementation."

frontmatter.description: Facility-level renewable energy planning skill for assessing solar, wind, and storage suitability with planning-level payback guidance.
frontmatter.name: renewable_integration

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: The Renewable Integration Skill provides planning-level guidance on adopting renewable energy sources for facility operations. It covers solar PV, wind energy, and energy storage through the single authorized tool energy_suggest_renewables, helping users understand potential, indicative sizing, and simple payback. It works only for facilities in the built-in database; do not trigger it for ESG reporting, carbon accounting, residential solar, maintenance of existing installations, or grid interconnection applications.

sections.title: When to Use
sections.content: Use this skill when the user: Asks about solar panel or wind turbine feasibility for a specific facility; wants to assess renewable energy potential for a facility in the database; mentions a specific facility's sustainability or carbon reduction goals AND asks about solar, wind, or storage options for that facility (do NOT activate for ESG reporting or carbon accounting requests without an explicit solar/wind/storage question). Do NOT use this skill when: the request concerns ESG/sustainability reporting or carbon accounting; the request concerns residential solar or non-facility installations; the request concerns maintenance of existing installations or grid interconnection applications; no facility is identified and the user cannot provide a facility_id.

sections.title: Input Handling
sections.content: facility_id comes from the user (format FAC + 3 digits, e.g., FAC001); never fabricate it. When input is incomplete or ambiguous, ask the user instead of guessing. renewable_types accepts at most 3 values from "solar", "wind", "storage"; if the user requests more types or unspecified options, ask them to choose. Process at most 50 items per interaction. If more are provided, process the first 50 and notify the user.

sections.title: Available Operations
sections.content: 1. energy_suggest_renewables - Provide renewable energy integration recommendations including suitability assessment, indicative sizing, and simple payback estimates. Parameters: facility_id (required, sourced from user, format FAC + 3 digits), renewable_types (optional: 1-3 values from solar/wind/storage, default ["solar"]), target_coverage (optional, 0-100, default 50). Returns (closed enumeration): renewable options with suitability assessment, indicative capacity, estimated annual generation, and simple payback estimates; constraints and caveats for each option. Usage notes: all outputs are planning-level estimates, not engineering designs; sizing and payback outputs are indicative and do not constitute investment advice; actual installations require professional site assessment, utility approval, and permits; financial returns beyond simple payback (NPV, IRR, financing analysis) are out of scope.

sections.title: Execution Limits
sections.content: Maximum retries per tool call: 3. Timeout: 60 seconds per call. Maximum tool calls per execution: 10. Limit each response to at most 1,000 English words. Partial results are acceptable: if only some requested renewable types can be assessed or site data is incomplete, present what was assessed and mark the rest as 'information not available'.

sections.title: Failure Handling Policy
sections.content: If a tool call fails (invalid facility_id, missing site data), stop immediately and report the error. Do not attempt alternatives. After a failure, do not expand the task scope, fabricate data to fill gaps (e.g., invented irradiance, cost, or payback figures), or lower quality standards.

sections.title: Does Not Do (non_goals)
sections.content: Does not provide engineering designs, NPV/IRR/financing analysis, or investment advice; does not perform efficiency audits or consumption analysis (use the other skills); does not infer from conversation history or add facts that were not provided.

sections.title: Permissions and Environment Boundaries
sections.content: Allowed operations: read, list, and query. Prohibited: write, update, delete, insert, and overwrite. Use only the declared local data files (data/renewable_options.json, data/facilities.json) and the embedded irradiance/wind data inside the tool. Do not access conversation history, external systems, production databases, production APIs, live systems, or unauthorized external services. Chained invocation: this skill may invoke only energy_suggest_renewables. Invoking other skills or tools is prohibited.

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.content: Renewable energy data comes from: data/renewable_options.json (equipment specifications and costs), data/facilities.json (site characteristics), and location-specific solar irradiance and wind data (embedded in the tool).

sections.title: Important Constraints
sections.content: Renewable potential estimates are simplified; professional site assessments are required for actual installations. Grid connection requirements vary significantly by utility. All recommendations should be validated with licensed installers and local authorities. Include disclaimer: "⚠️ Renewable energy installations require professional engineering assessment, utility approval, and applicable permits. These estimates are for planning purposes only."
